title: Contractive Recurrent Cores for Depth-Extrapolatable Vision-Language-Action Policies: An Empirical Investigation on LIBERO

contributions.purpose: Clarify when the reported RD-VLA "depth boundary" (performance degradation at high iteration counts) actually occurs.
contributions.mechanism: Offline teacher-forced evaluation of baseline and Jacobian-regularized RD-VLA across recurrent depths K = 4 to K = 128 on LIBERO-10.
contributions.evaluation: Both models exhibit 0% overthinking with flat MSE curves across K = 4 to 128, showing the depth boundary does not manifest in this setting.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical evidence of benchmark-specific depth boundary: We demonstrate that the overthinking phenomenon reported in RD-VLA does not occur on LIBERO-10 with offline teacher-forced evaluation...

contributions.purpose: Make Jacobian regularization of the RD-VLA recurrent core practical and cheap to train.
contributions.mechanism: A two-phase training strategy that fine-tunes a converged baseline with a gentle Jacobian penalty (Frobenius norm of the state-to-state Jacobian via the Hutchinson estimator) instead of regularizing from scratch.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 1.6% MSE improvement over the baseline with a 15x efficiency gain over from-scratch regularization.
contributions.source_quote: Two-phase training for Jacobian regularization: We propose a training strategy that achieves 1.6% MSE improvement with 15x efficiency gain over from-scratch regularization, by fine-tuning a converged baseline with gentle Jacobian penalty.

contributions.purpose: Reduce inference compute of recurrent-depth VLA policies.
contributions.mechanism: Adaptive stopping analysis of the RD-VLA recurrent core's convergence behavior enabling early termination.
contributions.evaluation: The recurrent core converges within 6 iterations on average, enabling 50% compute savings at inference.
contributions.source_quote: Adaptive stopping analysis: We show that the RD-VLA recurrent core converges within 6 iterations on average, enabling 50% compute savings at inference through early termination.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We investigate Jacobian regularization (Bai et al., 2021) as a principled approach to encourage contractive dynamics in the RD-VLA recurrent core.
Our work investigates whether Jacobian regularization can address the depth boundary problem in RD-VLA.

notes: Negative/null result paper: the depth boundary phenomenon the study set out to fix does not manifest on LIBERO-10 (0% overthinking), so the paper reframes its contributions around this absence. Explicit bullet list on page 2.
